slice: 3 of 3 (course end): u09, u10, u11, u12, p3, halbtest-sd1 — plus the whole-level story arc u01 → Halbtest

reviewers.persona: lizenzierte Prüferin Goethe-Zertifikat A1: Start Deutsch 1 — Prüfungstreue, Aufgabenklarheit, Schlüssel
Kursleiterin DaF A1.1 — Natürlichkeit, Niveau, Didaktik, Szenenplausibilität, Kontinuität

method: Read every German string of the six files (dumped per file), plus u08 (unit before) and the a1.2-u01 spec (unit after), the A1 cast bible (casts/a1.json, series.json), grammar-spine.json, lanes/sd1.json and the story beats/cliffhangers of u01–u12. Solved every authored item of the slice blind from promptDe + options/tiles/audio line (u09 ≈ 97, u10 ≈ 100, u11 ≈ 95, u12 ≈ 100, p3 14 + 5 form fields, Halbtest 17 + 5 form fields); no wrong key found. Graded all 934 answer/accepted strings of the 413 items with the real grader (src/lib/course-v2/checkItem.js): 0 fail. Ran 34 further candidate answers through checkItem; the misses are quoted in the findings. Recomputed every price and time chain (u09 bill 20,90 / 8,90 / 11,10 / 9,20; u10 9.10→10.25 and 18.35→19.50 = 1 h 15; u11 +60 min → ‚um neun‘): all consistent. Ran node scripts/course-v2/validate.mjs a1.1: 43 rules, 0 blocker; for these files only advisories/ratchets (GRM-02 recycling of g.moegen/g.wollen — waits for A1.2 specs; GRM-04 heuristic hits on Redemittel labels; LEX-01 labels/Aussprache focus; LEX-02 recurrence of u09/u10 lemmas — structurally expected at the end of the level, A1.2 must recycle; LEX-03 u09 checklist ‚Geburtstag‘ is a read surface, a false positive; TXT-01 three u12 exam sentences of 13–16 words). No official Modellsatz text was found copied; all exam texts are original and story-bound. No content was edited.

findings.where: units/u11.json spec.grammar.new[0] (g.perfekt-haben) with steps[0].pool.items[2] (a1.1-u11-ls1-p03), steps[0].pool.items[3] (p04), steps[0].reserve[1] (r02), steps[2].pool.items[0..3] (ls3-p01…p04), check.items[1] (a1.1-u11-c02), steps[5].task.leitpunkte[0], steps[0].microOutput.targets, steps[1].microOutput.targets; units/u12.json spec.grammar.new[0] (g.perfekt-sein) with steps[0].pool.items[0..3,9] (ls1-p01…p04, p10), check.items[0] (a1.1-u12-c01), check.items[3] (a1.1-u12-c04), steps[0].microOutput.targets; registries/grammar-spine.json g.perfekt-haben.intro.productive = a1.2-u05, g.perfekt-sein.intro.productive = a1.2-u08
findings.issue: Criterion (4): the spine makes the Perfekt productive only in A1.2 (haben U5, sein U8), but u11/u12 grade it productively: typed participles from the infinitive (gesehen, gearbeitet, gekauft, gegessen, gelesen, getrunken, gemacht, gespielt), typed/chosen auxiliaries incl. the haben/sein choice (u12 ls1-p04, p10, c04), both in the Lektions-Check, and the u11 S2 Leitpunkt ‚was haben Sie gemacht?‘ plus Sp2 cards in the Perfekt. The micro-outputs whose models are all Perfekt are targeted at g.zeitangaben-inversion (u11 mo1–mo3) and g.verbposition-2 (u12 mo1), so GRM-02's ‚productive target before intro.productive‘ check never fires, and GRM-04 treats a declared point as licensed — a gate hole. Net effect for the learner: three new grammar systems (Perfekt haben, Perfekt sein with auxiliary choice, wollen) in the last two units before the Halbtest, while BLUEPRINT §2.8 row 11/12 plans ‚Vergangenheit als Chunks (8–10 Formen)‘ and ‚Wiederholung‘.
findings.fix: Decide once, in the spine (owner of grammar-spine.json), then align the gate. Recommended (matches BLUEPRINT row 11, Menschen A1 L11–12, Schritte plus Neu 1 L7): set g.perfekt-haben.intro.productive = "a1.1-u11" with the label note „A1.1: feste Liste – gemacht, gekauft, gespielt, gekocht, gearbeitet, gegessen, getrunken, gesehen, gelesen, geschlafen, gelacht; das System ab a1.2-u05“, and g.perfekt-sein.intro.productive = "a1.1-u12" with „A1.1: gekommen, gefahren, geflogen, geblieben“. Then set u11 steps[0].microOutput.targets = ["g.perfekt-haben"], steps[1].microOutput.targets = ["g.perfekt-haben", "g.zeitangaben-inversion"], u12 steps[0].microOutput.targets = ["g.perfekt-haben", "g.verbposition-2"], and extend GRM-02 so that a typed item (fill_blank/error_correction/sentence_building) whose topic is a spine point counts as productive use. If the spine stays at A1.2 instead: drop a1.1-u11-c02, a1.1-u12-c01 and a1.1-u12-c04 from the Checks (replace with choice items: „Welcher Satz sagt: Das war gestern?“) and move u12 ls1-p04/p10 (haben oder sein?) to the reserve with banks ["mehr-ueben"] only.

findings.issue: „Am Mittwoch um ___ Uhr ist Elif am Park.“ — checkItem grades „17.00“ and „17:00“ WRONG (only „17“ and „5“ are accepted). „um 17.00 Uhr“ is standard written German and a defensible answer.
findings.fix: accepted → ["17", "5", "17.00", "17:00"], acceptedWhy add „17.00“/„17:00“: „auch richtig: 17.00 Uhr ist 17 Uhr“.

findings.issue: Tiles [fahren, Sie, auch, nach Dresden]: checkItem grades „Fahren auch Sie nach Dresden?“ WRONG, although u09 ls1-p09 accepts the exact parallel „Mögt auch ihr Kuchen?“ (reviewerConfirmed). A learner taught in u09 that this order is right is marked wrong one unit later.
findings.fix: accepted → ["Fahren Sie auch nach Dresden?", "Fahren auch Sie nach Dresden?"], acceptedWhy „Fahren auch Sie nach Dresden?“: „grammatisch: „auch“ vor „Sie“ betont „Sie“ (auch Sie, wie wir); das Verb bleibt auf Position 1“.

findings.issue: Inconsistent acceptance across adjacent units: u11 accepts the fronted non-finite verb in 12 sentence-building items („Gekocht habe ich am Sonntag.“, „Kommen kann ich am Mittwoch.“ — acceptedWhy „grammatisch, aber stark betont“), but u12 grades the same construction WRONG (checked: „Gekommen bin ich nach Leipzig.“, „Geblieben ist Emre in İzmir.“, „Arbeiten will ich in Leipzig.“, „Finden will Bilal Arbeit.“, „Machen wollen wir die Prüfung.“).

Recommended (never mark grammatical German wrong): add to accepted, with u11's acceptedWhy wording „grammatisch, aber stark betont: das Partizip/der Infinitiv auf Position 1, das Verb bleibt auf Position 2“ — ls1-p05 „Gekommen bin ich nach Leipzig.“, ls1-p06 „Geblieben ist Emre in İzmir.“, ls1-p07 „Gefahren sind wir mit dem Zug.“, ls1-p09 „Gefahren ist Frau Schulz nach Wien.“, ls1-r02 „Geblieben sind Emre und Arta in İzmir und Prishtina.“, ls2-p05 „Arbeiten will ich in Leipzig.“, ls2-p06 „Machen will Arta die Prüfung.“, ls2-r02 „Finden will Bilal Arbeit.“, c03 „Machen wollen wir die Prüfung.“. arc: u01–u12 + P3 + Halbtest read as one believable, well-paced story: first day and registration (u01–u02) → family and Arjun (u03) → saving and moving to Kölner Straße 18 (u04–u05) → laptop (u06) → day and doctor (u07) → Emre links Priya to Elif, running group (u08) → café after the run, Olena's birthday booking (u09, P3 chat) → Dresden with Sophie the day after the party, delayed train home (u10) → Monday weekend talk, postcard (u11) → last week, plans, A1.2 registration, internship e-mail (u12) → Halbtest set in the same world (Emre's e-mail, Frau Schulz's breakfast, Herr Richter's message) → a1.2-u01 opens exactly on the internship Monday. Every cliffhanger pays off in the next Folge; names, phone numbers (0176 38 29 41 06), address, ages, du/Sie relations and the u09 prices/u10 times match the cast bible and each other. The only arc breaks are the two majors above (Sophie's ‚nur einmal im Monat‘, Priya ‚arbeitet in Kochi‘) and the four minor fact drifts (café hours, Paula's time, Dresden fare, museum closing day).
verdict: Yes, this end of A1.1 is good enough to show learners once a short fix list is done: the story arc from u01 to the Halbtest is coherent and lively, the German is clean and natural, every one of the 413 items has a correct key (934 answer strings grade correct), and all Start-Deutsch-1 blocks, the Plateau and the Halbtest are format-correct and original. Before the owner plays it, fix the two story breaks a careful learner will notice (Sophie ‚sees her parents once a month‘, the Halbtest model ‚In Kochi arbeite ich am Empfang‘) and add the handful of correct answers the grader still rejects (17.00, „Fahren auch Sie …“, the fronted participles u11 accepts but u12 rejects). The one real decision is grammatical: u11–u12 teach the Perfekt productively while the grammar spine says A1.2, so the owner should confirm the Menschen/Schritte-style end of A1.1 and the spine should follow — none of this needs rewriting, it is about a day of edits.
